candidate_triage_2026_09_26.primary_identity: Honjo K, Tracey WD Jr. PLoS Genet. 2018;14(7):e1007464. PMID 30001326; PMCID PMC6042685.
candidate_triage_2026_09_26.primary_locator: PLOS full text: Results ‘Elevated BMP signaling increases Ca2+ responses in nociceptor terminals’, Fig. 6A-E (especially 6B-D); Results ‘Elevated BMP signaling in nociceptors induces behavioral nociceptive hypersensitivity’, Figs. 5A-B and 7A-E; Methods ‘Calcium imaging’, ‘Thermal nociception assay’ and ‘Optogenetic nociception assay’.

candidate_triage_2026_09_26.behavior_detail: Larval nocifensive escape locomotion (360-degree roll), measured as latency or response probability after heat or optogenetic activation; these operational endpoints do not measure subjective pain.
candidate_triage_2026_09_26.selection_rationale: Among three full-text candidates independently prioritized in Pi triage, this uniquely combines a Hiw-BMP/pMad sensitization mechanism, stimulus-evoked optical calcium responses at nociceptor terminals, and behavioral sensitization. Exact DOI is absent from records.json; this remains one of 18 DOI-unmatched works in the independent 28-work list.
candidate_triage_2026_09_26.claim_boundary: Calcium fluorescence is an optical physiological response, not an electrophysiological recording; pMad is a pathway reporter. No subjective-pain, human, clinical, or SCS inference. The historical aggregate 27 remains independently unreconciled.
